column5: Repeat clean-water power/load/intervention baseline before and after abuse tests
column6: Post-test clean-water performance change <=10% unless damage is intentionally induced
column7: Establishes whether later losses are real or just setup drift

column5: Run fine mineral sediment challenge at proposed accelerated concentrations 0.1, 1, and 5 g/L; then short sand pulses with ~100–500 µm washed silica; concentrations are screening challenges, not site claims
column6: No uncontrolled jam; sensors remain readable; after flush, recover >=90% of pre-test function or document service action/time
column7: Kills tiny passages, precision gaps, seals, optics, valves, and false-clean-water designs

column5: Operate over instrumented mobile sand/gravel bed; photograph/scan bed before/after; repeat with a sacrificial anchor/hub model
column6: No loss of required clearance or anchor function; quantify scour hole/deposition and any exposed/buried cable risk
column7: Seabed hardware changes local flow and can undermine or bury itself

column5: Introduce controlled neutrally/positively buoyant branch surrogates one at a time under guarded lab conditions
column6: No fragment ejection or uncontrolled runaway; machine reaches safe state and is recoverable; record power/load transient
column7: High-flow events often bring woody debris when loads are already high

column5: Introduce weed/rope/bag surrogates; include long flexible strips that can wrap rather than strike
column6: No permanent entanglement without a documented recovery method; quantify lost power and cleanout time
column7: A machine can become a trash rack even if nothing breaks

column5: Controlled monofilament, braid, light rope, and net-mesh coupons presented one at a time; no people near moving specimen
column6: Record snag probability, wrapping length, shutdown behavior, removal time; prefer geometry that sheds line rather than winds it
column7: Fishing gear is both a human-interaction and wildlife-entanglement pathway

column5: Use inert flexible fish-shaped/sensor-fish-like bodies of multiple sizes and trajectories; high-speed video and force/pressure instrumentation where available
column6: Measure collision/near-miss, peak acceleration/pressure/shear, trapping and clear passage; do not translate surrogate data directly into biological injury claims
column7: Pre-live-animal mechanical exposure screen; supports later ecological study design

column5: Apply repeatable roughness/attachment surrogates to blades, foils, ports, sensors and docking faces; separately deploy passive settlement coupons in field when permitted
column6: Quantify power/drag/sensor/docking degradation and cleaning time; establish trigger for service
column7: Tests whether modest colonization breaks performance before real long-duration trials

column5: After wet test, fully drain; cycle representative materials/components through 140°F/60°C water for 10 s and 120°F/49°C for 2 min; inspect seals, polymers, adhesives, coatings, magnets, labels
column6: No trapped-water volume inaccessible to drain/decon; no material/function failure after repeated decon cycles
column7: Minnesota portability requires design for clean/drain/decon, not just normal operation

column5: Wet components, deliberately include worst-case residual water; cycle freezing and thawing in controlled chamber; inspect dimensional change, cracks and seal damage
column6: Drainable design shows no freeze damage; any non-drainable cavity must prove freeze tolerance or be eliminated
column7: Tiny trapped volumes can destroy housings and become AIS reservoirs

column5: Cold-water/slush screening rig or specialized partner test; expose guards, inlets, flexible structures and sensors to ice-particle/slush surrogate
column6: No claim of overwinter capability until passed; initial product defaults to seasonal retrieval
column7: Frazil/anchor ice is sticky in supercooled turbulent freshwater and is notorious around hydraulic structures

column5: Use benign visible tracer fluid; sever/loosen one branch and measure released volume, isolation, continued operation and cleanup
column6: One branch failure does not drain entire shared circuit; released inventory is bounded and recoverable; no hazardous chemistry in early field units
column7: Multifunctional fluid is a liability if a torn leaf dumps the whole system into the lake

column5: Disable all electrical power, batteries, radios and software; add representative fouling/ballast; recover using only passive markers/recovery hardware and planned boat/winch procedure
column6: Recover without diver under target prototype conditions; record time, people, peak line force and number of special tools
column7: Real failures do not politely leave telemetry and actuators working

column5: Cycle loaded tether/cable over representative fairlead/bend/bed contact; include sediment; inspect sheath and strength
column6: No exposed conductor/fiber; quantified replacement interval and bend-radius rule
column7: Tether is simultaneously structure, debris collector, habitat surface, and cable

column5: Bench/field drill for unauthorized tie-off, hook snag, prop/anchor interaction scenarios; evaluate marking and physical deterrence
column6: No single casual tie-off or hook snag causes unsafe release; site/marking plan identifies residual hazards
column7: Humans will treat a visible buoy as a mooring and an invisible device as nonexistent

column5: Occlude camera, clog pressure port, roughen current sensor, induce encoder dropout; run conventional and relational diagnostics in shadow mode
column6: Unsafe state is not inferred from a single fouled sensor; contradictions stay visible; quantify false-trip/missed-fault behavior
column7: Environmental instrumentation itself fouls and lies

column5: Humidity/thermal cycles, cable-wicking check, low-pressure immersion/pressure cycling as appropriate
column6: No damaging condensation path; leak indicator catches ingress before functional loss
column7: Many 'waterproof' boxes fail from breathing, wicking and pressure cycling rather than obvious holes

column5: Accelerated UV/material coupon exposure; bird-perching/guano geometry review; rain/spray tests
column6: Surface materials/antennas remain serviceable; no critical vent/drain relies on staying clean
column7: Surface buoys live in sun, spray, ice, and bird shit, not CAD
